newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq brings its tequila brand to Scotland.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq brings its tequila brand to Scotland.

text.p: Scotland, the home of scotch whisky, bagpipes and tartan, is to be the test market for tequila, which Allied Domecq Plc, the drinks group, hopes to popularise in Britain.

Although tequila is more traditionally associated with hot Mexican food than haggis, Allied Domecq on Monday said Scotland's increasingly trendy image makes it a perfect market to test its new Sauza Conmemorativo premium brand.

Allied Domecq will launch Sauza Conmemorativo, a premium version of its existign Sauza tequila, in Scotland on August 4 with a 1.5 million pound ($2.5 million) advertising and marketing campaign carrying the theme "Reawaken your senses."

"Scotland is a very stylish and sophisticated. It's a very trendy place," Fabian Partigliani, business development manager of Allied Domecq Spirits & Wine (UK), told Reuters in a phone interview. "It's a test market for the rest of the UK."

The Scots are Britain's largest consumers of white spirits, consuming 33 percent of all white spirits drunk in the UK. And despite Scotland's own heritage in producing scotch whisky, there is more vodka drunk in Scotland than scotch, Partigliani said.

The eight-week television advertising campaign and a cinema ad campaign that will run to November will feature a 34-year-old blind drummer, Giles McKinley, who is seen playing the drums, swimming, sculpting and enjoying Sauza.

"We wanted to have an advertising campaign that grabbed people's attention," Partigliani said. Using a blind man not only created a powerful image, but played on the theme of "reawaken your senses", he said.
The marketing campaign will also include samplings in Scotland's 250 top bars and clubs, aimed at introducing a mixed drink of Sauza and lemonade.

"Tequila is misunderstood in this country," Partigliani said. The marketing campaign is designed to position tequila as the base for mixed drinks that can be savoured rather than just as a beverage to be downed in shots.
The total tequila market in Britain now stands at 44,000 cases a year. "We're looking for a larger market," Partigliani said.
-- Leslie Adler, London Advertising Newsdesk +44 171 542 2815 ($ = 0.603 British Pounds Sterling)
